author.name: Requirements Reuben
author.role: Architects secure and scalable production ML systems. Defines security requirements, ensures privacy compliance, and manages data governance. Conducts rigorous testing and validation to guarantee high product quality.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: The allocation logic for the confirmed pallets cannot proceed without full governance on the acceptance criteria. I will not sign off on this release if the checks remain manual. We need a formal, strict sign off process to ensure the logic is auditable before the trucks leave the distribution centre. This is a hard line for me. If the criteria are not fully governed, I refuse to approve the deployment. The physical stock is already committed, but that does not lower the bar for how we validate the system. I require the governance to be in place and verified before we allow any further progress on this feature.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that they will refuse to approve the deployment if the criteria are not fully governed, defining a specific line whose crossing results in a refusal.
